title: Modality-Agnostic Zeroth-Order LoRA Fine-Tuning for Black-Box Prompt Optimization

problem.claim: Prompt optimization for generative models is commonly a black-box optimization problem when model gradients are inaccessible in Model-as-a-Service settings.

gap.claim: White-box soft-embedding prompt optimization methods require gradients and therefore cannot be applied to black-box APIs.

contributions.claim: A modality-agnostic black-box prompt enhancement framework optimizes additional parameters within LoRA and can collaborate with white-box prompt optimization methods.
The Zeroth-Order LoRA Optimization method fine-tunes an open-source LLM to automatically optimize hard prompts for use with a black-box target model.
The method establishes an O(1/T) convergence rate with theoretical guarantees.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe their black-box prompt enhancement framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On Text-to-Image and Text-to-Text tasks, the method reportedly outperforms manually crafted prompts and baseline models on automated metrics and human preference ratings.
The method reportedly maintains a smaller parameter size while performing across diverse generation tasks.
Code is reported as available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative models can produce high-quality content from text prompts.
Prompt optimization becomes black-box when gradients are inaccessible, while white-box methods require gradient access.
The proposed framework applies zeroth-order optimization to LoRA parameters and hard prompts for black-box target models.
Experiments on Text-to-Image and Text-to-Text report improvements over manual prompts and baselines with fewer parameters.
The authors report that code is available.
